newsitem.title: USA: Dime to buy BFS for $91.8 million.
newsitem.headline: Dime to buy BFS for $91.8 million.

text.p: Dime Bancorp Inc. said on Tuesday it agreed to acquire BFS Bankorp Inc. for $52 per share in cash, or a total value of about $91.8 million.
BFS is the parent company of Bankers Federal Savings FSB, which operates five branch offices in the New York City boroughs of Manhattan, Queens and Brooklyn.

Dime, the parent of The Dime Savings Bank of New York, said the acquisition, which it expected to immediately add to earnings, was one of three actions taken to strengthen the company's balance sheet and earnings.
Dime said it will also reduce its mortgage-backed securities portfolio by $1.2 billion, with no loss expected, and it planned to buy back up to 5 percent of the company's outstanding common stock.
The company has about 106.4 million shares outstanding.

In the portfolio reduction, Dime said it plans to sell a total of $950 million of mortgage-backed securities. It would reduce its portfolio by an additional $300 million by not reinvesting the proceeds of maturing securities.
Dime said it expects the BFS merger to be completed in the second quarter of 1997.
